title: publish-runtime-performance-surface-and-version-stability-api
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Define and publish a new API surface that explicitly exposes model runtime capabilities and performance profiles used for version pinning and routing decisions. The goal is to provide downstream consumers (Console, Dedicated router, SDKs, and customers) with a machine-readable contract: token and context limits, latency/throughput performance buckets, quantization and kernel compatibility hints, and version stability metadata for safe pinning and fallbacks.

Problem: Current model manifests are inconsistent across onboarding paths and lack structured, release-stable fields for performance and stability. This causes: accidental regressions when serving falls back to incompatible variants, opaque routing decisions, and manual intervention for enterprise customers that want to pin to stable model versions with known latency characteristics.

Proposed API: 1) GET /v1/models/{model_id}/runtime-profile?version={semver or tag} - returns profile_v1 fields: model_id, version, context_window, token_limits (per-request & per-minute), perf_buckets (p50_ms, p95_ms, tokens_per_second), memory_estimates (cpu_mb, gpu_mb), quantization_profiles (list), kernel_affinities (list), recommended_batching (min_batch, max_batch, tradeoffs), stability_score (0-100), pinned_until (date or null), compatible_variants (list of variant ids), feature_flags (list of supported features e.g., streaming, function-calls, structured-output). 2) POST /v1/models/{model_id}/profiles/publish - internal-only endpoint for onboarding pipelines to publish profile artifacts and provenance (CI job id, benchmark harness link, commit sha). 3) GET /v1/models?capability=embedding&max_latency_ms=200 - filter endpoint for consumers to discover models matching constraints.

Compatibility: profile_v1 must be additive to existing manifest endpoints. We will maintain manifest_v2 for a transition window and provide a migration script to generate profile_v1 from current benchmarks where available. Old clients continue to use /models/{id}/manifest but will be encouraged to shard routing based on the new profile fields.

Acceptance criteria: - API schema documented in OpenAPI and Console UI surfaces use profile fields for instance-level routing decisions. - SDKs (python/js) add convenience accessors for perf_buckets and stability_score. - Onboarding pipeline writes a profile artifact during CI that links to the benchmark run. - E2E tests verifying fallback behavior when a pinned version is removed or marked unstable.

Rollout plan: Stage 1 (internal) - deploy read endpoints and publish profiles for a small set of widely used open models. Stage 2 (console+SDK) - surface data in Console and add routing hints in Dedicated router. Stage 3 (customer) - invite select customers to use version pinning with stability_score gating. Stage 4 - deprecate legacy manifest-only routing after 3 months of adoption.

Telemetry & Metrics: track API read latency, profile publication success/failure, number of models with valid perf profiles, and routing incidents where fallback occurred due to missing or incompatible profiles.

Documentation & links: Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/XYZ-PerfProfile-Design  , Benchmark harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/142 , Draft OpenAPI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-specs/pull/87
